info.title: Fashlab Studio — Customer API
info.description:
Customer-side REST API for the Fashlab Studio mobile app.

### There are no customer accounts
The app mirrors the website: a visitor browses, fills in the checkout form and orders as a guest. There is no registration, no sign-in and no order history. The only login anywhere is the admin panel on the website, which this API does not expose.

An order is reached afterwards by its **order number plus the email or phone used on it** — `/orders/track` — which is what the site's track-order page does.

### Start here
1. **POST `/session`** — returns a device token. It is not a credential; it just carries the cart and wishlist, because a phone has no session cookie. Click **Authorize** above and paste it in.
2. Browse `/home` and `/products`, add to `/cart`, save to `/wishlist`.
3. **POST `/orders`** with the form fields to place the order.

If a request arrives with no token, or a stale one, a fresh token is issued and returned in the **`X-Api-Token`** response header — read that header on every response and replace your stored token when it differs.

### Every response has the same shape
```json
{ "success": true, "message": null, "data": { }, "errors": { } }
```
Branch on `success`, show `message` to the customer, and map `errors` (`{"field": "message"}`) straight onto form validators on a 422.

### Base URL
This webspace applies mod_rewrite patterns but drops the substitution — the same reason the storefront serves `/product.php?slug=…` instead of pretty permalinks — so the API routes on `PATH_INFO` and the base URL ends in `/index.php`. `…/index.php?_route=products` works too, and needs no server support at all.

### Notes
- Prices come back pre-formatted (`"Rs. 6,050"`); the app does no money maths.
- Image URLs are absolute.
- Payment is **Cash on Delivery only** — no gateway is connected.
- If a host strips `Authorization`, send the token in `X-Api-Token` instead.
- No CSRF token is needed.

post.description:
**Call this on first launch and store the token.**

This is not a login — there are no customer accounts. The token is an anonymous device identity that carries the cart and the wishlist between requests, because a phone has no session cookie.

Safe to call on every launch: presented with a valid token it returns that same token rather than starting a new cart.

get.description: One call for the whole home screen, so it paints in a single round trip.
Accepts a slug or a numeric id. Also records the view and the recently-viewed entry.

post.description: Name and email are typed in by the reviewer, as there are no accounts. Reviews are held for moderation before they appear, exactly as on the website.

patch.description:
Body form. Prefer this over the path form — a cart key contains a colon, which some clients and proxies mangle in a URL path.

A quantity of 0 removes the line.

422.description: Coupon not valid for this cart

post.description:
Validity, minimum order and usage limits are all checked server-side.

`WELCOME10` in the example is a placeholder — replace it with a code that exists in Admin -> Coupons, or the response is a 422 saying the code is not valid.

post.description:
Guest checkout, exactly like the website: fill in the form and order. There is no account.

Prices, shipping and the coupon are recalculated server-side — anything the client sends about money is ignored.

**Keep `order_number` from the response.** With no account, that number plus the email or phone is the only way back to the order.

**Payment is Cash on Delivery only.** No gateway is connected, so a card order could never be settled.

404.description: No order matches that number and contact

post.description: `contact` must be the email or phone used on the order. Requiring it is what stops an order number on its own from exposing someone's address.

get.description: The same lookup as `/orders/track`, for deep links and for polling an order just placed. `contact` is required for the same reason.
